tasks.short: Encourage one student with feedback that builds confidence.

steps.what: Read the praise card before this feedback.
outputs: one stuck skill and one thing that went well

steps.what: Provide feedback to students using positive reinforcement techniques to encourage, motivate, or build confidence in students.
inputs: one stuck skill and one thing that went well

tasks.design: A praise card lists the subject, the last stuck skill, and the one thing that went well. The classroom teacher or a teaching assistant writes it before the session. The tutor reads it, then still encourages the student in the room. If the card has no row, the tutor reads the paper note in the same step. The card does not encourage the student.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last stuck skill and the one thing that went well sat in a long note the tutor hunted before speaking.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the subject, the last stuck skill, and the one thing that went well is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing words that encourage this student, and judging whether the praise is true today, stays with the tutor.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor hears the student and decides what confidence to build in the room.
tasks.altitude: The tutor still encourages the student. The card only shortens finding the last praise.

reach.role: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
reach.task: Encourage a pupil after class work
reach.learn: Read the subject, the last stuck skill, and the one thing that went well, then still encourage the pupil.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the subject, the last stuck skill, and the one thing that went well shortens the search when the row is there. The tutor still encourages the student. Model knowledge.

AI that admits learners, evaluates learning outcomes, or monitors tests in educational institutions is high-risk from 2 December 2027. This paper card does none of that. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex and the cited date.

tasks.short: Review class material by working problems with a student.

steps.what: Read the page card before this review.
Review class material with students by discussing text, working solutions to problems, or reviewing other assignments.

tasks.design: A page card lists the subject, the assignment title, and the page. A teaching assistant writes it before the review. The tutor reads it, then still discusses the text and works the problems with the student. If the card has no row, the tutor reads the paper assignment in the same step. The card does not review the material.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assignment title and the page sat in a stack of papers the tutor hunted before the review.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the subject, the assignment title, and the page is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Discussing the text and working the problems with this student stays with the tutor.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor sees where the student stalls and chooses the next question.
tasks.altitude: The tutor still reviews the material with the student. The card only shortens finding the page.

tasks.short: Assess progress during one tutoring session.

steps.what: Read the topic card before this tutoring session.
Assess students' progress throughout tutoring sessions.
Write the progress note after the session.

tasks.design: A topic card lists the subject and the last page. The classroom teacher writes it before the session. The card does not hold a grade. The tutor reads it, assesses progress with the student, then writes the progress note by hand after the session. If the card has no row, the tutor reads the paper note in the same step. The card does not assess the student.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last page sat in a long note the tutor hunted before assessing progress.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the subject and the last page is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Judging this student's progress throughout the session stays with the tutor, and the written note stays a hand note.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor hears the answers and decides what progress to record.
tasks.altitude: The tutor still assesses progress and still writes the note. The card only shortens finding the last page.

tasks.short: Teach study skills and test-taking strategies.

steps.what: Read the skill card before this study-skills session.
Teach students study skills, note-taking skills, and test-taking strategies.

tasks.design: A skill card lists the subject, the one skill, and one example. A teaching assistant or the classroom teacher writes it before the session. The tutor reads it, then still teaches the skill. If the card has no row, the tutor reads the paper plan in the same step. The card does not teach the student.

tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the subject, the one skill, and one example is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the skill to this student, and choosing the example that fits, stays with the tutor.
tasks.human_edge: The tutor watches the student try the skill and changes the example.
